input.summary:
H2 loft is furnished as an attic drying loft: a spruce drying table (slab top, fence legs, pots and a focal lantern) with stair chairs at z 12/14, barrel stores with lanterns, a drying campfire on a hay stack, and standing lanterns in the south lane.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with 28 room-8 blocks placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `room --rooms rooms-build.json` says OK: 164/164 cells reachable, 0 dark, min light 6, 8 dim cells left.
Rendered room.png (from above and inside) reads as a drying loft. Structure check shows no floating or unsupported blocks in this part; the 3 orphan slabs at y6 belong to other parts.
left: No checklist row in plan.md or elements.md covers the H2 loft room, so nothing was ticked.
8 of 164 floor cells are still dim (light 1-7), at x14 z13 and x19 z21; the tool's suggested lanterns there would lift them, but I left them out to keep the lanes open.
The 3 orphan smooth_stone_slab blocks at y6 (x 11, 19, 31, z 9) are outside this part and belong to the frontage or shell parts.
Furniture and stair-foot clearance were checked only with mcd room and a look at room.png, not with a separate mcd walk run.

waste.what: Worked out the room's cell coordinates by hand and typed each furniture row as text; I had to convert plan.md's floor rows into layer rows indexed from z 8, with column 0 at x 13.
waste.cost: About 15 text rows across 3 layers and 3 corrections after a wrong index, plus one re-run of make.sh.
waste.tool: A plan output that prints the layers() rows with the correct origin and shows a blank template per layer, so the furniture text can be filled in place.

waste.what: Spent time finding out why the furniture was missing from the room check. The `mcd room` command was given rooms.json (world y) and not rooms-build.json (file y, shifted by YOFF), so the walk and the floor grid read the wrong storey.
waste.cost: One full debug pass: a dump of build.nbt cells, a check of the layer coordinates, and a re-run with the shifted rooms file.
waste.tool: `mcd room` and `mcd plan` should detect the YOFF shift themselves, or the brief should say to pass rooms-build.json for every check after make.sh.

waste.what: Checked by hand that the lantern light levels and the focal piece's brightness were right, by reading the light grid and the tool's suggestions.
waste.cost: Two make.sh rebuilds and one room check, about 3 minutes.
waste.tool: `mcd room` could print a per-cell light map and suggest which lantern moves fix the dim cells, so one run is enough.

companions.task: Place the lanterns for the last 8 dim cells (x14 z13 and x19 z21) and pick lantern spots that keep the lanes open, so the 8+ light rule holds without a second pass.
